q: When bodies are immersed in a liquid there is loss in weight due to a property of liquids called _____.
e: When bodies are immersed in a liquid there is loss in weight due to a property of liquids called buoyancy. Viscosity or surface tension is not this quantity.

q: Since buoyant force is directed upward, it is called _____.
e: Buoyant force is the upward push of the fluid, equal to the weight of the displaced fluid. Since buoyant force is directed upward, it is called upward thrust. Downward thrust or lateral thrust is not this quantity.

q: Archimedes' principle states that the upward thrust acting on a body which is immersed in a liquid is equal to the _____ of the liquid displaced by the body.
e: Archimedes' principle: the upthrust equals the weight of fluid displaced. Archimedes' principle states that the upward thrust acting on a body which is immersed in a liquid is equal to the weight of the liquid displaced by the body. Volume or mass is not this quantity.

q: Archimedes' principle is true not only for liquids but also for _____.
e: Archimedes' principle: the upthrust equals the weight of fluid displaced. Archimedes' principle is true not only for liquids but also for gases. Do not trade gases for solids or plasmas.

q: The weight of a body when it is immersed in a liquid is called _____ weight.
e: The weight of a body when it is immersed in a liquid is called apparent weight. Actual or true is not this quantity.

q: The apparent weight of a body is less than the actual weight because of the _____ of the liquid acting on it.
e: The apparent weight of a body is less than the actual weight because of the upward thrust of the liquid acting on it. Do not trade upward thrust for downward thrust or friction.

q: If the weight of the body is greater than the upward thrust, the body will _____.
e: If the weight of the body is greater than the upward thrust, the body will sink. Do not trade sink for float or rise.

q: If the weight of the body is smaller than the upward thrust, the body will rise up to the _____.
e: If the weight of the body is smaller than the upward thrust, the body will rise up to the surface. Do not trade surface for bottom or middle.

q: A body will float in a liquid if the upward thrust acting on it is equal to its _____.
e: A body will float in a liquid if the upward thrust acting on it is equal to its weight. Volume or density is not this quantity.

q: For a floating body, the ratio of the densities is equal to the ratio of the immersed volume to the volume of the _____.
e: For a floating body, the ratio of the densities is equal to the ratio of the immersed volume to the volume of the whole body. Displaced liquid or container is not this quantity.

q: The volume of a totally immersed block is equal to the volume of liquid _____ by the block.
e: The volume of a totally immersed block is equal to the volume of liquid displaced by the block. Do not trade displaced for absorbed or evaporated.

q: The forces acting on the sides of a totally immersed block _____.
e: The forces acting on the sides of a totally immersed block cancel out. Do not trade cancel out for add up or increase.

q: The net force acting on a totally immersed block in the upward direction is called the _____ force.
e: The net force acting on a totally immersed block in the upward direction is called the buoyant force. Gravitational or frictional is not this quantity.

q: The densities of various substances can be obtained by using _____ principle.
e: The densities of various substances can be obtained by using Archimedes' principle. Pascal's or bernoulli's is not this quantity.

q: If a body is in equilibrium while floating, the net force acting on it is _____.
e: If a body is in equilibrium while floating, the net force acting on it is zero. Maximum or minimum is not this quantity.
